==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|growe||archaic}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|growen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|grōwan|t=to grow, increase, flourish, germinate}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*grōan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*grōaną|t=to grow, grow green}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*gʰreh₁-|t=to grow, become green}}.
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|nl|groeien|t=to grow}}, {{cog|nds-de|grojen|t=to green; thrive; take hold; flourish}}, {{cog|da,nb,nn,sv|gro|t=to grow}}, {{cog|fo|grógva|t=to grow}}, {{cog|is|gróa|t=to grow}}; also {{cog|la|grāmen|t=grass, turf; herb, plant}}, {{m|la|herba|t=grass, herbage; weeds; plant}}, {{cog|uk|гря́ний|t=green}}. Related to [[growth]], [[grass]], [[green]].
{{col-bottom}}

* {{hyph|en|grow}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|+|+|grew,~ed<l:dialectal>|n,~ed<l:dialectal>}}

# {{lb|en|ergative}} To [[become]] [[larger]], to [[increase]] in [[magnitude]].
#: {{ux|en|Children '''grow''' quickly.}}
# {{lb|en|ergative|of plants}} To [[undergo]] [[growth]]; to [[be]] [[present]] {{gloss|somewhere}}.
#: {{syn|en|range<qq:flora>}}
#: {{ux|en|Apples now '''grow''' all over the world. The tallest trees '''grow''' to about 30 feet.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[appear]] or [[sprout]].
#: {{ux|en|Leaf buds '''grew''' on the trees with the advance of spring.}}
#: {{ux|en|A long tail began to '''grow''' from his backside.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[develop]], to [[mature]].
#: {{ux|en|As I '''grew''' throughout adolescence, I came to appreciate many things about human nature.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To cause or allow something to become bigger, especially to [[cultivate]] plants.
#: {{ux|en|He '''grows''' peppers and squash each summer in his garden.}}
#: {{ux|en|Have you ever '''grown''' your hair before?}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2023-07-10|author=w:James Poniewozik|title=The Twitter Watch Party Is Over|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/10/arts/television/tv-twitter-end-of-an-era.html|passage=And — again to overgeneralize from my experience — users may not want a second Twitter either. I was a heavy Twitter user for over a decade. I loved it until I didn’t. I made connections, '''grew''' a following, floated ideas, had fun. But it also became a second, often angry, voice inside my head. Do I want to replace it with another one?|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250817110526/https://www.nytimes.com/2023/07/10/arts/television/tv-twitter-end-of-an-era.html|archivedate=17 August 2025}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}<!-- Please no more than 3–4 quotes here, further quotes only in 'Citations' (see [[WT:QUOTE]])-->
# {{senseid|en|become}} {{lb|en|copulative}} To [[assume]] a condition or quality over time.
#: {{par|en|become<id:copulative>|get<id:become>|go<id:become>|turn<id:become>|come<id:become>|fall<id:become>|wax<id:become>}}
#: {{ux|en|The boy '''grew''' wise as he matured.}}
#: {{ux|en|My cares '''grew''' less ([[less and less|and less]]) until they evanesced completely.}}
#: {{ux|en|You have '''grown''' strong.}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}<!-- Please no more than 3–4 quotes here, further quotes only in 'Citations' (see [[WT:QUOTE]])-->
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To become attached or fixed; to adhere.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 2|V|iii|passage=Our knees shall kneel till to the ground they '''grow'''.}}
#* {{see more citations|en}}<!-- Please no more than 3–4 quotes here, further quotes only in 'Citations' (see [[WT:QUOTE]])-->
